title: Extended Car Warranties: An Expensive Gamble
summary: Consumer Reports' survey of 12,000 extended-warranty buyers found most never used the coverage, and those who did often still lost money net of cost.

assertions.quote: 55 percent of owners who purchased an extended warranty hadn't used it for repairs during the lifetime of the policy
those who did use it spent hundreds more for the coverage than they saved in repair costs
the most satisfied were primarily owners of less reliable brands

verdicts.note: Directly reported in Consumer Reports' survey comparing brands like BMW and Mercedes-Benz against Honda and Toyota.

assertions.quote: that costs more money in the long run, however, because you have to pay interest on the warranty's fee
Most of those who did haggle were successful, saving about $325 on average
respondents who purchased automaker-backed coverage through a dealership were substantially more satisfied

verdicts.note: Matches Consumer Reports' survey finding higher satisfaction for automaker-backed coverage.

assertions.quote: The impression they want to give people is that they are contacting them on behalf of their dealer or manufacturer
they're informed that pre-existing conditions don't apply
an extended warranty might be worth considering if you're planning to keep your vehicle long after the factory warranty runs out
